risks: No participants; the risk is a misleading synthesis that drives or blocks funding.
consent: Not applicable: published reviews only; no new data are collected from patients.
data: No personal data; the citation matrix and appraisal sheets are archived with the report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: people with complex needs, in deprived areas, from minority ethnic groups or with severe mental illness may benefit differently. The overview extracts subgroup and mechanism findings for these groups and states where reviews are silent.
effectiveness: Useful if the board can see which outcomes have credible evidence and which do not.
efficiency: Uses protected GP time and analyst support; no data collection.
partnerships: Link workers, two people who have used social prescribing, and the voluntary sector forum.
rebPath: No research ethics review is required for an overview of published reviews; the report goes to the commissioning board.
limitations: Depends on the quality and reporting of existing reviews; mainly one reviewer; published data only.
summary: Overview of published reviews with an equity focus on complex needs and deprivation.
